funFact: De Bazel on Vijzelstraat was built in 1919-26 as the head office of the Nederlandsche Handel-Maatschappij, to a design by K.P.C. de Bazel, who died in 1923 before it was finished. A concrete frame is clad in brick banded with granite, which earned the ten-storey Amsterdam School block the nickname 'De Spekkoek' (layer cake). Sculptures over the entrance honour J.P. Coen, H.W. Daendels and J.B. van Heutsz. It has housed the city archives (Stadsarchief Amsterdam) since 2007.
